summary: A World War II double-gable corrugated-metal heavy warehouse east of the Machine Shop, framing the Historic Core's plaza with Building 2; the smallest of Orton's eight Historic Core buildings, rehabilitated with a new mezzanine and seismic bracing (certificate of occupancy August 2017) and subleased whole to Obscura Digital (The Madison Square Garden Company) for seven years from September 2017.

milestones.text: Built as the Heavy Warehouse for equipment used in Machine Shop 1 and ship outfitting (NRHP date; the Port's documents say 1944)
Port Commission endorses the Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan (Resolution 10-27), which calls for a National Register district and rehabilitation of the 20th Street buildings

Port Commission awards the 20th Street Historic Buildings opportunity to Orton Development after a 2011 RFP; Exclusive Negotiating Agreement approved April 2012; term sheet endorsed October 2012 (Board of Supervisors December 2012)

Historic Preservation Commission informational hearing on the rehabilitation of the ten 20th Street Historic Buildings (case 2013.1168E): ~270,000 gsf existing plus ~69,000 gsf of new mezzanines, ~334,000 gsf total
Union Iron Works Historic District listed in the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 14000150), giving the project access to federal historic tax credits
Port Commission Resolution 14-33 approves the Lease Disposition and Development Agreement and 66-year Master Lease (L-15814) with Historic Pier 70, LLC (Orton) and adopts CEQA findings
Master lease approved by the Board of Supervisors and fully executed, giving Orton site control; construction commences thereafter (September 2015 per the National Trust)
Permanent financing for the Historic Core project achieved

Port Commission update: six of eight buildings complete, Buildings 101 and 102 still under construction, project 100% subleased except two atrium retail spaces; total cost revised from $81.9M to an estimated $127.0M
Historic Shipyard at Pier 70 Rehabilitation receives a Governor's Historic Preservation Award
Obscura Digital reported with a 22,000 sq ft lease in the Historic Core
Sublease to Obscura Digital / The Madison Square Garden Company commences: entire building, seven years, PDR use
First occupancy of Buildings 14 and 104 'this summer' anticipated in the Port's September 2017 briefing

costs.what: Hard cost of the Building 14 rehabilitation (2018 actual; $2.6M at 2014 approvals)

facts.value: Orton Development, Inc. through Historic Pier 70, LLC (66-year master lease L-15814 from the Port of San Francisco)
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects (design architect); Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture (historic architect)

Developer equity up to $14 million plus loans; Port participation rent of 50% of revenues above debt and a 14% equity return; sources in 2018: Port capital $1.8M, Seismic Safety Loan $23.6M, historic tax credit equity $20.4M, private debt and equity $81.2M
Contributing resource to the Union Iron Works Historic District (NRHP, listed April 17, 2014)
1941 (NRHP nomination); 1944 per the 2013 HPC packet and the Port's 2019 memo
140 ft by 116 ft 6 in by 66 ft tall, double-gable metal building clad in corrugated galvanized iron, with a 20-ton crane
15,969 (NRHP); 16,315 before and 25,215 after rehabilitation (Port); 23,000 sq ft per the contractor
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects; IwamotoScott (contractor's credit)
Full interior and exterior renovation, new mezzanine, seismic bracing, restrooms, kitchen and office spaces, and a light-industrial workshop for a digital production company
Obscura Digital / The Madison Square Garden Company (entire building, from September 2017, seven-year term)
Heavy warehouse; storage for the Port's maintenance division before rehabilitation
Forms a courtyard with Building 2 and the 113/114/115/116 complex; the ~45,000 sq ft plaza is publicly accessible

open_questions: Obscura Digital's seven-year sublease from September 2017 would have ended around 2024; no source names the current occupant.
The construction date conflict (1941 in the NRHP nomination vs 1944 in the Port's documents) is unresolved; the nomination's date is used in the summary.
Building 14 sits on the same Assessor lot as Building 2 and the shipyard (4052001); this record follows the repo's split of Building 14 from that lot.
